name: Environmental Justice Legislative Table
description: Statewide coalition of community-based, environmental, Indigenous and civil rights organizations, led by grassroots and community-of-color-led groups, formed in 2019 to support and influence environmental justice legislation and policy in Massachusetts.

name: Springfield Climate Justice Coalition
description: Coalition of roughly 60 community, faith, labor, health and environmental groups in the Springfield area, formed in 2014, that works on climate and environmental health issues; it fought the East Springfield biomass plant, opposes new gas pipeline expansion, and won a city Climate Action and Resiliency Plan.

name: Green Justice Coalition
description: Partnership of community-based building nonprofits and labor organizations that grows the power of working-class people and people of color in the Greater Boston area and beyond. Its work includes energy democracy and grid modernization, project labor agreements for public infrastructure, and public transit equity.
members: Greenroots Environmental Chelsea Organizers Youth Crew

name: Climate Resilient Schools Coalition
description: Coalition organizing for climate-resilient, equitable school infrastructure investments.

name: HERO Coalition
description: Coalition of housing advocacy and environmental organizations working for statewide solutions to the climate and affordable housing crises. It backs legislation to raise the Massachusetts deeds excise fee and split the revenue between affordable housing and climate investments.
members: Jewish Alliance for Law and Social Action

name: Vermont Environmental Common Agenda
description: Annual shared legislative agenda issued by Vermont Conservation Voters and 21 partner organizations covering democracy, resilient communities, transportation, food security, toxic-free communities and affordable clean energy. The 2026 edition (22 partners) came out Jan 14, 2026.

name: Energy Action Network
description: Montpelier-based network of 200+ nonprofits, businesses, public agencies and other organizations working toward Vermont's climate and energy goals; staff act as neutral convener and it publishes the annual Progress Report for Vermont. All non-profit members on its member page are linked here (VECAN and Vermont Clean Communities are modelled as separate coalitions, and the Vermont Housing Finance Agency is left out as a state agency); its business, utility, higher-education and public-sector members are omitted.
members: Champlain Valley Office of Economic Opportunity
Building Performance Professionals Association of Vermont
Climate Economy Action Center of Addison County
New England Grassroots Environment Fund (Grassroots Fund)

name: Vermont Energy & Climate Action Network
description: Network of 100+ Vermont town energy committees (since 2005) and the organizations that support them, coordinated by VNRC with Energy Action Network, Efficiency Vermont, Vital Communities and the Vermont Council on Rural Development. Its committee map is interactive, so only committees whose VECAN directory page appeared in public search results are linked.

name: #ActOnClimateVT
description: Coalition of 30+ Vermont organizations that builds support for equitable, just climate solutions; it says it helped pass the 2020 Global Warming Solutions Act.

name: Transportation for Vermonters
description: Cross-sector coalition convened by VNRC pushing for a sustainable, accessible, affordable transportation system in a rural state; launched in Nov 2017 and still testifying to the legislature in Feb 2026.

name: Vermont Clean Communities (Clean Cities Coalition)
description: Burlington-based U.S. DOE Clean Cities coalition (designated since 2001) that works on clean, efficient transportation access through stakeholder partnerships. About 80 stakeholders are listed, mostly businesses, utilities, towns and agencies; only the nonprofit/advocacy ones with verified details are linked.

name: Vermont Environmental Justice Network
description: Statewide network that connects overburdened community members, especially BIPOC and other frontline Vermonters, with decision-makers on environmental and climate justice. It runs community listening sessions, sets legislative priorities and held a two-day EJ Summit in Montpelier in June 2026.
